explanation: The same `summary` object is created once outside the loop and pushed into `results` on every iteration. Since objects are stored by reference, all entries in `results` alias the exact same object — by the time the loop finishes, every element in `results` reflects the final accumulated totals and items list, not a per-order snapshot. Each iteration needs a fresh object (e.g. a shallow copy) pushed instead.
prompt: Why does every entry in `results` end up showing the same final totals instead of per-order snapshots?
choices: The same `summary` object is aliased and pushed into `results` each iteration, so all entries end up referencing the final accumulated state
`summary.total` is never initialized before the loop, causing `NaN` to accumulate
The loop should use a classic `for (let i = 0; i < orders.length; i++)` instead of `for...of` to avoid this
`results.push(summary)` should be `results.push(summary.total)` since only the numeric total is needed downstream
